title: 'Lou and His Ginger Snaps' and why those tunes were recorded
summary: Asked about a September 13, 1929 session, he says the Savoy first billed Russell as the Ginger Snaps and that the tunes were outside material Russell was asked to record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Charlie Holmes (10/31/82):
...Luis Russell recording from September 13, 1929, and it's "Broadway Rhythm" and "The Way He Loves Is Just Too Bad." These were issued as Lou and His Ginger Snaps. Do you remember that recording?
Sure.
Can you tell me something behind that name of "Lou and His Ginger Snaps."
No, except that the only thing... It must have been Luis Russell and his Ginger Snaps. That's the only thing I know about the name.
Didn't you say the Savoy gave him the name of Ginger Snaps.
Well, yeah. The Savoy is the first one I know that had it up in the lights, "Luis Russell and His Ginger Snaps." Why they did it, I don't know.
But it was something, then, that was associated with Russell and not something that was just thought up by the studio that issued the...
No-no-no. It was Luis Russell's name as far as the Savoy was concerned. It was the first one that I've seen use it, "Luis Russell and the Ginger Snaps."
Well, see, these were issued for another company other than Okeh, so he probably didn't want his whole name associated with that.
Holmes (10/31) - 2
Mmm-hmm.
Do you remember why these particular tunes were picked?
No. Why they were picked, this-that-and-the-other, I don't know.
"Broadway Rhythm" and "The Way He Loves Is Just Too Bad", were they numbers that were part of the regular Russell repertoire?
No. They were something come up for a recording.
And that might have been the only time you played those numbers?
Well, after we recorded them, we kept them in the book. After they was recorded, we kept them in the book.
Because they're not compositions by anybody in the band.
No. We never heard them before we recorded them.
So I guess Russell must have been asked to do those numbers.
Apparently, yes. Definitely.
Because most of the numbers of the Russell band, it seems to me, were from members of the band or...
That's true, or him.
Holmes (10/31) - 3
Or Russell's own.
That's right.
